beats.say: Richard Rodgers was the first person to win an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony.
The American composer received his fourth distinct award in 1962.
Helen Hayes was the first woman and the first performer to win all four.
Puerto Rican actress, dancer, and singer Rita Moreno received her fourth distinct award in 1977.
Only one person, Robert Lopez, has won all four awards twice.
English actor and theatre director John Gielgud received his fourth distinct award in 1991.
The EGOT acronym was coined by actor Philip Michael Thomas in late 1984.
